cond_0001.intro:
A Postdoctoral Research Associate position is open in the Department of Medicine, Division of Oncology, Center for Gene and Cellular Immunotherapy at [Company name masked]. Our lab works at the interface of immune cells within the hematopoietic system with the goal of mobilizing these to safely and effectively attack cancer. We use a variety of techniques including in vitro cell culture, primary human and mouse immune cell isolation, lentiviral and retroviral gene transfer, CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, a variety of in vivo mouse models, and single-cell genomics to investigate the interactions of T cells and their immune environment. We ultimately aim to enhance long-term survival for human patients using cell and gene therapy approaches.
We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher interested in working on genetically modified hematopoietic stem cells and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells for treatment of hematologic malignancies. The postdoctoral researcher will work with human and mouse hematopoietic stem cells to investigate how to best utilize these in the context of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and CAR T cell therapy. The candidate will have the opportunity to engage in research across a broad range of fields including stem cell biology, immunology, cancer biology, and cell and gene therapy according to their interests.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Trains under the supervision of a faculty mentor including (but not limited to):
Manages their own project, which should lead to a first author publication.
Develops expertise in flow cytometry, genetic manipulation of mouse and human immune cells, in vitro cytotoxicity assays, and in vivo mouse models.
Develops proficiency in career skills, including writing, presenting, networking, and critical evaluation of scientific literature.
Presents scientific work both inside and outside the University.
Assists with grant preparation and reporting.
Prepares and submits papers.
Designs research experiments and collects data.
Maintains compliance with good laboratory practice including the maintenance of adequate research records.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
PhD or equivalent in biomedical sciences
Good spoken and written communication skills
Preferred Requirements
Research experience in cancer biology and/or immunology
Experience with flow cytometry
Experience with mouse models

cond_0035.intro:
A Postdoctoral Research Associate position is open at [Company name masked] in the Department of Medicine, Division of Oncology, Center for Gene and Cellular Immunotherapy. Our lab works at the interface of immune cells within the hematopoietic system with the goal of mobilizing these to safely and effectively attack cancer. We use a variety of techniques including in vitro cell culture, primary human and mouse immune cell isolation, lentiviral and retroviral gene transfer, CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, a variety of in vivo mouse models, and single-cell genomics to investigate the interactions of T cells and their immune environment. We ultimately aim to enhance long-term survival for human patients using cell and gene therapy approaches.
We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher to take ownership of research on genetically modified hematopoietic stem cells and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells for treatment of hematologic malignancies. The postdoctoral researcher will lead work with human and mouse hematopoietic stem cells to determine how to best utilize these in the context of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and CAR T cell therapy. The candidate will direct research across a broad range of fields including stem cell biology, immunology, cancer biology, and cell and gene therapy according to their interests.
cond_0035.responsibilities:
Trains under the supervision of a faculty mentor including (but not limited to):
Owns and manages their own project, which should lead to a first author publication. Builds expertise in flow cytometry, genetic manipulation of mouse and human immune cells, in vitro cytotoxicity assays, and in vivo mouse models. Develops proficiency in career skills, including writing, presenting, networking, and critical evaluation of scientific literature. Presents scientific work both inside and outside the University. Contributes to grant preparation and reporting. Prepares and submits papers. Designs research experiments and collects data. Maintains compliance with good laboratory practice including the maintenance of adequate research records.
cond_0035.requirements:
Applicants should have a PhD or equivalent in biomedical sciences.
The ideal candidate will have research experience in cancer biology and/or immunology, flow cytometry, and mouse models.
All applicants should have good spoken and written communication skills.
This position works in a laboratory environment with potential exposure to biological and chemical hazards. The individual must be physically able to wear protective equipment and to provide standard care to research animals.
Interested applicants should send 1) a one-page cover letter briefly describing their previous research experience and future career goals, 2) a curriculum vitae, and 3) contact information of 2-3 references to the hiring contact.
All external candidates receiving an offer for employment will be required to submit to pre-employment screening for this position. The screenings will include criminal background check and, as applicable for the position, other background checks, drug screen, an employment and education or licensure/certification verification, physical examination, certain vaccinations and/or governmental registry checks. All offers are contingent upon successful completion of required screening.

A Postdoctoral Research Associate position is open in the Department of Medicine, Division of Oncology, Center for Gene and Cellular Immunotherapy at [Company name masked]. Our lab works at the interface of immune cells within the hematopoietic system with the goal of mobilizing these to safely and effectively attack cancer. We use a variety of techniques including in vitro cell culture, primary human and mouse immune cell isolation, lentiviral and retroviral gene transfer, CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, a variety of in vivo mouse models, and single-cell genomics to investigate the interactions of T cells and their immune environment. We ultimately aim to enhance long-term survival for human patients using cell and gene therapy approaches.
We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher interested in working on genetically modified hematopoietic stem cells and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells for treatment of hematologic malignancies. The postdoctoral researcher will work with human and mouse hematopoietic stem cells to investigate how to best utilize these in the context of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and CAR T cell therapy. The candidate will have the opportunity to engage in research across a broad range of fields including stem cell biology, immunology, cancer biology, and cell and gene therapy according to their interests. Most people become stronger in this kind of research over time as they build hands-on experience and learn from feedback in the lab.
cond_0068.responsibilities:
Trains under the supervision of a faculty mentor including (but not limited to):
Manages their own project, which should lead to a first author publication. Develops expertise in flow cytometry, genetic manipulation of mouse and human immune cells, in vitro cytotoxicity assays, and in vivo mouse models. Develops proficiency in career skills, including writing, presenting, networking, and critical evaluation of scientific literature. Presents scientific work both inside and outside the University. Assists with grant preparation and reporting. Prepares and submits papers. Designs research experiments and collects data. Maintains compliance with good laboratory practice including the maintenance of adequate research records.
cond_0068.requirements:
Applicants should have a PhD or equivalent in biomedical sciences.
The ideal candidate will have research experience in cancer biology and/or immunology, flow cytometry, and mouse models.

This position works in a laboratory environment with potential exposure to biological and chemical hazards. The individual must be physically able to wear protective equipment and to provide standard care to research animals.

cond_0080.intro:
We are looking for a Postdoctoral Research Associate to join our team at [Company name masked] in the Department of Medicine, Division of Oncology, Center for Gene and Cellular Immunotherapy. Our lab works at the interface of immune cells within the hematopoietic system with the goal of mobilizing these to safely and effectively attack cancer. We use a variety of techniques including in vitro cell culture, primary human and mouse immune cell isolation, lentiviral and retroviral gene transfer, CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, a variety of in vivo mouse models, and single-cell genomics to investigate the interactions of T cells and their immune environment. We ultimately aim to enhance long-term survival for human patients using cell and gene therapy approaches.
We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher to lead work on genetically modified hematopoietic stem cells and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells for treatment of hematologic malignancies. The postdoctoral researcher will drive research with human and mouse hematopoietic stem cells to determine how to best utilize these in the context of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and CAR T cell therapy. The candidate will own a research agenda spanning stem cell biology, immunology, cancer biology, and cell and gene therapy according to their interests.

Develops and applies career skills, including writing, presenting, networking, and critical evaluation of scientific literature.
Presents scientific work both inside and outside the University.
Contributes to grant preparation and reporting.
Prepares and submits papers.
Designs research experiments and collects data.
Maintains compliance with good laboratory practice including the maintenance of adequate research records.

cond_0270.intro:
A Postdoctoral Research Associate position is open in the Department of Medicine, Division of Oncology, Center for Gene and Cellular Immunotherapy at [Company name masked]. Our lab works at the interface of immune cells within the hematopoietic system with the goal of mobilizing these to safely and effectively attack cancer. We use a variety of techniques including in vitro cell culture, primary human and mouse immune cell isolation, lentiviral and retroviral gene transfer, CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, a variety of in vivo mouse models, and single-cell genomics to investigate the interactions of T cells and their immune environment. We ultimately aim to enhance long-term survival for human patients using cell and gene therapy approaches.
We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher to collaborate on work involving genetically modified hematopoietic stem cells and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells for treatment of hematologic malignancies. The postdoctoral researcher will work alongside colleagues using human and mouse hematopoietic stem cells to investigate how to best utilize these in the context of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and CAR T cell therapy. The candidate will have the opportunity to engage in research across a broad range of fields including stem cell biology, immunology, cancer biology, and cell and gene therapy according to their interests.
cond_0270.responsibilities:
Trains under the supervision of a faculty mentor including (but not limited to):
Coordinates with the lab to advance their own project, which should lead to a first author publication. Develops expertise in flow cytometry, genetic manipulation of mouse and human immune cells, in vitro cytotoxicity assays, and in vivo mouse models. Develops proficiency in career skills, including writing, presenting, networking, and critical evaluation of scientific literature. Shares scientific work through presentations both inside and outside the University. Assists with grant preparation and reporting. Prepares and submits papers in collaboration with the team. Works with colleagues to design research experiments and collect data. Supports compliance with good laboratory practice including the maintenance of adequate research records.
cond_0270.requirements:
Applicants should have a PhD or equivalent in biomedical sciences.
The ideal candidate will have research experience in cancer biology and/or immunology, flow cytometry, and mouse models.
All applicants should have good spoken and written communication skills.
This position works in a laboratory environment with potential exposure to biological and chemical hazards. The individual must be physically able to wear protective equipment and to provide standard care to research animals.
Interested applicants should send 1) a one-page cover letter briefly describing their previous research experience and future career goals, 2) a curriculum vitae, and 3) contact information of 2-3 references to the hiring contact.
All external candidates receiving an offer for employment will be required to submit to pre-employment screening for this position. The screenings will include criminal background check and, as applicable for the position, other background checks, drug screen, an employment and education or licensure/certification verification, physical examination, certain vaccinations and/or governmental registry checks. All offers are contingent upon successful completion of required screening.

cond_0353.intro:
A Postdoctoral Research Associate position is open in Dr. [Company name masked]'s Lab in the Department of Medicine, Division of Oncology, Center for Gene and Cellular Immunotherapy at [Company name masked]. Our lab works at the interface of immune cells within the hematopoietic system with the goal of mobilizing these to safely and effectively attack cancer. We use a variety of techniques including in vitro cell culture, primary human and mouse immune cell isolation, lentiviral and retroviral gene transfer, CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, a variety of in vivo mouse models, and single-cell genomics to investigate the interactions of T cells and their immune environment. We ultimately aim to enhance long-term survival for human patients using cell and gene therapy approaches.
We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher interested in working on genetically modified hematopoietic stem cells and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells for treatment of hematologic malignancies. The postdoctoral researcher will work with human and mouse hematopoietic stem cells to investigate how to best utilize these in the context of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and CAR T cell therapy. The candidate will have the opportunity to engage in research across a broad range of fields including stem cell biology, immunology, cancer biology, and cell and gene therapy according to their interests.

Assists with grant preparation and reporting. Prepares and submits papers. Designs research experiments and collects data. cond_0510.intro:
A Postdoctoral Research Associate position is open in the Department of Medicine, Division of Oncology, Center for Gene and Cellular Immunotherapy at [Company name masked]. Our lab works at the interface of immune cells within the hematopoietic system with the goal of mobilizing these to safely and effectively attack cancer. We use a variety of techniques including in vitro cell culture, primary human and mouse immune cell isolation, lentiviral and retroviral gene transfer, CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, a variety of in vivo mouse models, and single-cell genomics to investigate the interactions of T cells and their immune environment. We ultimately aim to enhance long-term survival for human patients using cell and gene therapy approaches.
We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher interested in working on genetically modified hematopoietic stem cells and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells for treatment of hematologic malignancies. The postdoctoral researcher will work with human and mouse hematopoietic stem cells to investigate how to best utilize these in the context of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and CAR T cell therapy. The candidate will have the opportunity to engage in research across a broad range of fields including stem cell biology, immunology, cancer biology, and cell and gene therapy according to their interests.
cond_0510.responsibilities:
Trains under the supervision of a faculty mentor including (but not limited to):
Manages their own project, which should lead to a first author publication.
Develops expertise in flow cytometry, genetic manipulation of mouse and human immune cells, in vitro cytotoxicity assays, and in vivo mouse models.
Develops proficiency in career skills, including writing, presenting, networking, and critical evaluation of scientific literature.
Presents scientific work both inside and outside the University, actively engaging with colleagues and broader scientific audiences.
Assists with grant preparation and reporting.
Prepares and submits papers.
Designs research experiments and collects data.
Maintains compliance with good laboratory practice including the maintenance of adequate research records.
cond_0510.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
PhD or equivalent in biomedical sciences.
Good spoken and written communication skills.
Preferred Requirements
Research experience in cancer biology and/or immunology, flow cytometry, and mouse models.
